steps: Learn sports vocabulary with correct genders for jouer à and faire de
Use jouer à for team / ball sports and faire de for individual activities
Know which verbs use être in the passé composé and how to agree the past participle
Practice describing past sporting events using the passé composé and frequency adverbs
method_card.title: Sport and Staying Active
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sport vocabulary, jouer à vs faire de, frequency adverbs, and the passé composé for talking about past sporting events.

FrenchEnglish
le footballfootball
le tennistennis
le basket(-ball)basketball
la natationswimming
le cyclismecycling
la gymnastiquegymnastics
l'athlétisme (m)athletics
l'équitation (f)horse riding
la musculationweight training
garder la formeto keep fit
participer àto take part in
passionnant(e)exciting
tous les samedisevery Saturday
trois fois par semainethree times a week

jouer à = to play (team sports and ball sports): jouer au foot (m → au), jouer à la pétanque (f → à la), jouer aux cartes (pl → aux). faire de = to do (individual sports and activities): faire du vélo (m → du), faire de la natation (f → de la), faire de l'équitation (vowel → de l').

Passé composé with être: Verbs of movement and change of state (aller, venir, arriver, partir, sortir, etc.) and all reflexive verbs use être as the auxiliary. The past participle agrees with the subject: Elle est allée (f), Ils sont allés (m.pl).

Model: Je joue au football tous les samedis avec mes amis et je fais de la natation le mercredi. L'année dernière, j'ai participé à un tournoi de tennis et c'était passionnant. Je fais du sport trois fois par semaine pour garder la forme. — I play football every Saturday with my friends and I do swimming on Wednesdays. Last year, I took part in a tennis tournament and it was exciting. I do sport three times a week to keep fit.

exam_context.frequency: Common across speaking and writing tasks — sport topics appear in every exam series

bullets.note: j'adore + definite article; parce que + opinion with justification

bullets.note: passé composé: j'ai participé à; c'était (imperfect for description)

bullets.model_answer: L'année dernière, j'ai participé à un tournoi de tennis. C'était fantastique !

bullets.note: near future: je vais + infinitive; polite question with est-ce que
bullets.prompt: Say what sport you are going to do this weekend and ask if the leisure centre has a pitch / court / pool.
bullets.model_answer: Ce week-end, je vais faire du cyclisme. Est-ce que le centre sportif a une piscine, s'il vous plaît ?

wrong.peux: peux is present tense. After si with a conditional result, use the imperfect: pouvais.
wrong.pourrais: You cannot use the conditional after si in French. Use the imperfect: pouvais.

gaps.correct_explain: pouvais is the imperfect of pouvoir. In si clauses hypothesising about the present, use the imperfect.

wrong.fais: fais is present tense. The result clause needs the conditional: ferais.
wrong.ferai: ferai is the simple future (-ai). The conditional has -ais: ferais.

gaps.correct_explain: ferais is the conditional of faire. The result clause of a si + imperfect structure uses the conditional. Irregular stem: fer- + -ais.

bronze.question: Match the French sports to the English meaning
Match the French sport phrases to the English meaning

wrong.fais du: Football is a team sport — use jouer à, not faire de.
wrong.joue de: The correct preposition for jouer with sports is à, not de.

gaps.correct_explain: joue au — football is a team sport → jouer à. Le football is masculine → au.

wrong.joue \u00e0 la: Swimming is an individual sport — use faire de, not jouer à.

gaps.correct_explain: fais de la — swimming is an individual activity → faire de. La natation is feminine → de la.

gaps.correct_explain: est is the elle form of être. Aller uses être in the passé composé.
sont is the ils form of être. Ils sont allés.

options: I love football because it is exciting
I hate football because it is boring

bronze.question: What does 'J'adore le football parce que c'est passionnant' mean?

misconceptions.message: You picked this because 'passionnant' sounds a bit like 'boring' in tone, but adore means love, not hate, and passionnant means exciting, not boring.
You picked this thinking passionnant meant easy, but it actually means exciting. Facile would mean easy, so this describes a different quality of the game.
You picked this because football often links to playing, but j'adore means I love, not I play, so the sentence is about feelings, not action.

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly uses faire de?

misconceptions.message: You picked this because à feels like a natural link word, but faire de always pairs with de la/du, not à, when talking about doing a sport.
You picked this mixing up jouer and faire, but gymnastics uses faire de la, since jouer is for games and instruments, not activities like this.
You picked this by dropping the 'de', but faire needs de la before a feminine noun like gymnastique to show you're doing that activity.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Jouer à = team sports and ball sports: jouer au foot, au tennis, au basket.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Faire de = individual sports and activities: faire de la natation, du cyclisme, de l'athlétisme.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Jouer à for team / ball sports, faire de for individual activities. Both need article contractions: au (m), à la (f), aux (pl) for jouer; du (m), de la (f), de l' (vowel) for faire.

worked_examples.question: When do you use jouer à vs faire de?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: aller is a verb of movement → it uses être (not avoir) in the passé composé.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: With être, the past participle agrees with the subject. Elle = feminine → add -e.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: She went to the stadium. The -e on allée shows agreement with the feminine subject elle.
